newsitem.title: GERMANY: Bayer enters rubber joint-venture in China.
newsitem.headline: Bayer enters rubber joint-venture in China.

text.p: German chemicals group Bayer AG said on Wednesday it planned a joint venture with Chinese group Sinopec Shanghai Gao-Ziao Petrochemical Corporation, valued at over $100 million, to manufacture synthetic rubbers.

In a statement Bayer said the two groups had signed a letter of intent on Wednesday and that more detailed negotiations would now begin. Investment for the first stage will be some $100 million, Bayer said.
The joint-venture would produce styrene-butadiene rubber and butadiene rubber for the Chinese market and for export, supplying tyre manufacturers as well as the plastics industry.

Sinopec is expected to transfer its 60,000 tonnes per annum butadiene rubber capacity to the joint venture and a new facility to produce 100,000 tonnes per annum of butadiene and styrene-butadiene is expected to be built.
Bayer added that the proposed contract also includes the option for a another 100,000 tonne per annum facility.
Bayer is already one of the world's leading suppliers of synthetic rubbers.
